title: Present Simple
summary: Habits, timetables, facts and things that are generally true.

rules.name: Form
rules.form: I / you / we / they + V  ·  he / she / it + V-s
rules.when: Positive sentences.

examples.en: I play football every weekend.
She plays the guitar.

rules.name: Negatives and questions
rules.form: do / does + not + V  ·  Do / Does + subject + V?
rules.when: After do/does the main verb never takes -s.

examples.en: He doesn't play chess.
Does she like drawing?

rules.name: Time expressions
rules.form: always · usually · often · sometimes · hardly ever · never · every day · on Mondays
rules.when: These words almost always go with the Present Simple.

examples.en: I hardly ever watch TV.
examples.uk: Я майже ніколи не дивлюсь телевізор.

mistakes.note: he / she / it → doesn't
after does, use the base form

quiz.q: She ___ (go) to the gym on Mondays.

practice.q: My brother ___ the guitar every evening.
practice.why: he / she / it takes -s in the Present Simple.
we takes the base form.
she → doesn't + base form.

practice.q: ___ your parents work at the weekend?
practice.why: your parents = they → Do.

practice.q: The shop ___ at nine every morning.
practice.why: A regular timetable takes the Present Simple, and the shop = it.
I → don't.

options: Does she goes to school by bus?
Does she go to school by bus?
Do she go to school by bus?
practice.why: After does the verb has no -s.
A general fact takes the Present Simple.
my friends = they → don't.
A verb ending in consonant + y changes to -ies.

title: Present Continuous
summary: What is happening right now, or around this period of your life.

rules.name: Form
rules.form: am / is / are + V-ing
rules.when: An action at the moment of speaking, or a temporary situation.

examples.en: I'm doing my homework right now.
He's learning to skateboard this month.
examples.uk: Цього місяця він учиться кататися на скейті.

rules.name: Time expressions
rules.form: now · right now · at the moment · today · this week
rules.when: A signal that the action is in progress, not a habit.

examples.en: Look! They're playing in the yard.

rules.name: State verbs
rules.form: like, love, hate, want, know, understand, need — no -ing
rules.when: State verbs are not used in the continuous form.

examples.en: I like this song. (NOT I'm liking)

mistakes.note: like is a state verb
don't forget am / is / are

quiz.q: I ___ this book at the moment.

options: I am wanting a new phone.
I am want a new phone.

practice.why: Look! points at this moment.
right now → am / is / are + -ing.

practice.q: They ___ in the garden at the moment.
practice.why: they → are.
know is a state verb — no Continuous.

practice.q: We ___ a new topic this week.
practice.why: this week = a temporary period.
The Continuous question starts with am / is / are.

practice.q: He ___ TV — he's doing his homework.
practice.why: A negative right now takes isn't + -ing.

practice.q: Sorry, I ___ dinner. Can I call you back?
practice.why: An action in progress at the moment of speaking.

practice.q: The kids ___ upstairs. Please be quiet.
practice.why: Happening now, so the Continuous.
want is a state verb.

title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
summary: The core question is simple: is this generally true, or is it happening around now?

rules.name: The one question to ask
rules.form: generally true → Present Simple  ·  happening around now → Present Continuous
rules.when: Ask yourself: would this still be true next month? If yes, it is a routine and takes the Simple.

examples.en: I walk to school. (every day, in general)
I'm walking to school. (right now, on my way)

rules.name: Time markers give it away
rules.form:
Simple: always · usually · every day · on Mondays · never
Continuous: now · right now · at the moment · today · this week
rules.when: Find the time expression first — it usually decides the tense for you.

examples.en: She usually wears jeans, but today she's wearing a dress.
examples.uk: Вона зазвичай носить джинси, але сьогодні вона в сукні.

rules.name: Both tenses in one sentence
rules.form: …usually + Present Simple, but + today / at the moment + Present Continuous
rules.when: This is the pattern that shows you really understand the contrast — use it in writing and speaking.

examples.en: I normally have breakfast at home, but this week I'm eating at school.
examples.uk: Зазвичай я снідаю вдома, але цього тижня я їм у школі.

examples.en: My brother plays football, but he isn't playing today — he's ill.
examples.uk: Мій брат грає у футбол, але сьогодні не грає — він хворий.

rules.name: Careful: state verbs
rules.form: know · like · want · need · understand · believe — Simple only
rules.when: Even when you mean right now, state verbs stay in the Simple. See the State verbs topic.

examples.en: I want to go home now. (NOT I'm wanting)

mistakes.note: Look! / Listen! point at this moment

mistakes.wrong: I'm going to school every day.
mistakes.right: I go to school every day.
mistakes.note: every day is a routine
state verb — Simple only

mistakes.wrong: What do you do right now?
mistakes.right: What are you doing right now?
mistakes.note: right now needs the Continuous

quiz.q: I usually drink tea, but today I ___ coffee.
What ___ at the weekend? — Nothing special, I stay at home.
Sorry, I can't talk — I ___ dinner at the moment.

practice.q: I usually ___ at seven, but today I ___ at nine.
practice.why: usually → Simple, today → Continuous.
Listen! points at this moment.

practice.q: My sister ___ in Lviv, but this month she ___ in Kyiv.
practice.why: A permanent fact takes the Simple, a temporary one the Continuous.
on Fridays is a routine.

practice.q: What ___ tomorrow evening? — Nothing, I'm free.
practice.why: An arrangement in the future takes the Continuous.

practice.q: He ___ meat, so make him a salad.
practice.why: A general habit takes the Simple.
be is a state verb: just is.

practice.q: She ___ French at school, and right now she ___ for a test.
practice.why: Routine first, action in progress second.
No -ing, no time marker of the moment — a routine.

practice.q: The bus ___ at 7:40 every day, but today it ___ late.
practice.why: A timetable takes the Simple; today's exception takes the Continuous.

title: Past Simple
summary: A finished action in the past — the main tense for telling stories.

rules.name: Form
rules.form: V-ed  ·  irregular verbs: go → went, break → broke
rules.when: The action happened and finished in the past.

examples.en: I started skateboarding two years ago.
examples.uk: Я почав кататися на скейті два роки тому.

examples.en: He fell off and broke his arm.

rules.name: Negatives and questions
rules.form: didn't + V  ·  Did + subject + V?
rules.when: After did, always use the base form.

examples.en: We didn't go out yesterday.
Did you win the match?

rules.name: Time expressions
rules.form: yesterday · last week · in 2020 · two days ago · when I was 10
rules.when: A specific moment in the past.

examples.en: I took up chess when I was ten.
examples.uk: Я почав грати в шахи, коли мені було десять.

mistakes.note: go is an irregular verb
after did, use the base form

quiz.q: She ___ come to the lesson yesterday.

practice.q: We ___ to the cinema last night.
practice.why: go is irregular: go → went.
lose → lost.
A past negative takes didn't + base form.
A past question starts with Did.

practice.q: I ___ my grandparents two weeks ago.
practice.why: ago points to a finished moment.

practice.q: He ___ a photo and ___ it to me.
practice.why: take → took, send → sent.
After did, use the base form.

practice.q: The film ___ at eight and ___ at ten.
practice.why: Both actions are finished in the past.

practice.q: I ___ tired, so I went to bed early.
practice.why: I → was.

practice.q: We ___ any milk, so I went to the shop.
practice.why: didn't + base form is the usual past negative.

title: Past Continuous
uk: actions in progress in the past
summary: An action that was in progress at a moment in the past — the background of a story.

rules.name: Form
rules.form: was / were + V-ing
rules.when: The action was in progress at a specific moment in the past.

examples.en: At 7 p.m. I was practising the guitar.
examples.uk: О 7-й вечора я тренувався на гітарі.

rules.name: while and when
rules.form: while + Past Continuous · when + Past Simple
rules.when: A long action is interrupted by a short one.

examples.en: While I was riding my bike, it started to rain.
examples.uk: Поки я їхав на велосипеді, почався дощ.

examples.en: I was playing football when I hurt my knee.
examples.uk: Я грав у футбол, коли забив коліно.

mistakes.wrong: While I rode my bike, I fell.
mistakes.right: While I was riding my bike, I fell.
mistakes.note: while → the longer action
we / you / they → were

quiz.q: I ___ (watch) a film when he called.
While she ___ dinner, the lights went out.

practice.q: At six o'clock yesterday I ___ dinner.
practice.why: An action in progress at a point in the past.

practice.q: They ___ football when it started to rain.
practice.why: The longer action takes the Past Continuous.
while → the longer action.

practice.q: We ___ for you at the station.
practice.why: we → were.

practice.q: I broke my arm while I ___ my bike.
practice.why: while + the action in progress.
An action in progress at that moment.

practice.q: He ___ TV when his mum came home.
practice.why: The background action takes the Continuous.

options: While I was walking, I met Anna.
While I walked, I was meeting Anna.
While I walk, I met Anna.
practice.why: while + Continuous, then the short action in the Past Simple.
Two background actions set the scene.

practice.q: They ___ talking when the teacher came in.
practice.why: they → were.

title: Past Simple: forms and spelling
summary: Regular -ed, irregular verbs, and the one rule that fixes most mistakes: no second form after did.

rules.name: Regular verbs
rules.form: verb + -ed
rules.when: Spelling: wait → waited · decide → decided · grab → grabbed · study → studied (but play → played).

examples.en: I waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
She grabbed her bag and ran.

rules.name: Negatives and questions
rules.form: didn't + infinitive · Did + subject + infinitive?
rules.when: The past is already inside did, so the main verb goes back to its first form.

examples.en: My alarm didn't go off.
What time did she get home?

mistakes.note: one past marker is enough — it is in did
same rule in questions
go is irregular
short vowel + one consonant: double it

quiz.q: I ___ for the bus for twenty minutes.
He ___ nothing and just looked at me.

practice.q: I ___ for the bus for twenty minutes.
practice.why: A regular verb just adds -ed: wait → waited.
Short vowel + one consonant: double it before -ed.
A verb ending in -e just adds -d.
Consonant + y → -ied.
Vowel + y keeps the y: play → played.
didn't + the base form.
A past question starts with Did.
After did the verb has no past form.

practice.q: He ___ nothing and just looked at me.
practice.why: say is irregular: say → said.
One past marker is enough — it sits in didn't.

title: while and when
uk: Past Simple разом з Past Continuous
summary: The long action is the background; the short one cuts across it.

rules.name: Background and event
rules.form: was / were + -ing  +  Past Simple
rules.when: Something was already going on when a short event happened.

examples.en: While I was waiting at the bus stop, a van soaked me.
examples.uk: Поки я чекав на зупинці, мене облив фургон.

examples.en: He broke his arm while he was playing basketball.
examples.uk: Він зламав руку, коли грав у баскетбол.

rules.name: Which word goes where
rules.form: while + long action · when + short event
rules.when: Both orders are possible; the tense tells you which action is which.

examples.en: I was reading when the lights went out.

rules.name: Two long actions together
rules.form: was/were + -ing  +  was/were + -ing
rules.when: Both actions lasted and happened at the same time.

examples.en: While I was cooking, my brother was playing video games.
examples.uk: Поки я готував, брат грав у відеоігри.

mistakes.wrong: While I walked home, I saw an accident.
mistakes.right: While I was walking home, I saw an accident.
mistakes.note: while marks the long action
they / we / you take were
state verbs never take the Continuous

quiz.q: While I ___ at the bus stop, a van soaked me.
It ___ to rain while we were walking home.
When the bell ___, everybody stood up.
While I was cooking, my brother ___ video games.

practice.q: While I ___ at the bus stop, a van soaked me.
practice.why: while marks the long background action.

practice.q: It ___ to rain while we were walking home.
practice.why: The short event that cuts in takes the Past Simple.
Asking about the action in progress at that moment.

practice.q: When the bell ___, everybody stood up.
practice.why: when + a short event.

practice.q: While I was cooking, my brother ___ video games.
practice.why: Two long actions at the same time — both Continuous.
they → were.

practice.q: I ___ my arm while I was playing basketball.
practice.why: The sudden event takes the Past Simple.

options: While I walked home, I saw an accident.
While I was walking home, I saw an accident.
practice.why: while needs the longer action in the Continuous.

practice.q: She ___ the answer, so she put her hand up.
practice.why: know is a state verb — never Continuous.

practice.q: I was reading ___ the lights went out.
practice.why: when introduces the short event.

title: Adverbs of frequency
summary: Where to put always, usually, often and never — and why that position is not random.

rules.name: The main rule
rules.form: before the main verb, but AFTER the verb to be
rules.when: always · usually · often · sometimes · hardly ever · never

examples.en: I always do my homework.
He is never late.

rules.name: With an auxiliary verb
rules.form: auxiliary + adverb + main verb
rules.when: When there is can, will, have, or am/is/are + -ing.

examples.en: She can usually help me.

rules.name: Frequency expressions
rules.form: once a week · twice a month · every day — at the start or end of the sentence
rules.when: These expressions never go in the middle of the sentence.

examples.en: We train twice a week.

mistakes.wrong: I go always to school by bus.
mistakes.right: I always go to school by bus.
mistakes.note: before the main verb
after the verb to be

options: in the middle of the sentence
at the start or at the end
I always am hungry after school.
I am always hungry after school.
Always I am hungry after school.
practice.why: After the verb to be.
Before a main verb.
The adverb goes before the main verb.

practice.q: He is ___ late for the lesson.
practice.why: hardly ever = almost never.

options: in the middle of the sentence
at the start or the end
practice.why: Time expressions are not placed mid-sentence.

practice.q: I ___ can help you on Sundays.
practice.why: auxiliary + adverb + main verb.

practice.q: They ___ watch TV in the morning.
practice.why: The adverb comes after the auxiliary in a negative.
twice a week is the fixed form.
With to be the adverb goes after the verb.

practice.q: My dad ___ drinks coffee in the evening.
practice.why: never is already negative — no second negative.

title: play / go / do
summary: Three verbs that go with different kinds of activity.

rules.name: play
rules.form: play + a ball game or a game with rules and an opponent
rules.when: football, basketball, tennis, chess, video games, the guitar

examples.en: They play basketball after school.
examples.uk: Вони грають у баскетбол після школи.

rules.name: go
rules.form: go + an activity ending in -ing
rules.when: swimming, running, cycling, skateboarding, shopping, fishing

examples.en: I go swimming twice a week.
examples.uk: Я ходжу плавати двічі на тиждень.

rules.name: do
rules.form: do + an individual activity without a ball
rules.when: yoga, karate, gymnastics, athletics, exercise, homework

examples.en: She does karate on Saturdays.

mistakes.note: -ing activities take go
martial arts take do

practice.why: A game with rules and an opponent takes play.
An -ing activity takes go.
Martial arts take do.
Musical instruments take play.
An -ing activity takes go.
An individual activity without a ball takes do.
Games take play.
An -ing activity takes go.
Individual sports without a ball take do.
An -ing activity takes go.

title: State verbs
summary: Verbs that describe a state, not an action. They are not used in the Continuous.

rules.name: What they are
rules.form: like · love · hate · want · need · prefer · know · understand · believe · remember · mean · cost · belong · seem
rules.when: These verbs describe a state you cannot film, so they stay in the Simple even when we talk about right now.

examples.en: I know the answer.
Do you need any help?

rules.name: Verbs that work both ways
rules.form: have · think · see · taste
rules.when: When the verb describes an action rather than a state, the Continuous is fine.

examples.en: I have a bike. / I'm having breakfast.
examples.uk: У мене є велосипед. / Я снідаю.

examples.en: I think you're right. / I'm thinking about it.
examples.uk: Я думаю, ти маєш рацію. / Я обмірковую це.

mistakes.note: know is a state — never in the Continuous
need is a state, so the question takes do/does

mistakes.wrong: She is wanting a new phone.
mistakes.note: want is a state

practice.why: understand is a state verb.
Here taste describes a quality, not an action.
want is a state verb.

practice.q: Be quiet — I ___ about the answer.
practice.why: Here think means the mental action, so the Continuous works.

practice.q: They ___ a big house in the village.
practice.why: have = own is a state.

practice.q: We ___ lunch — call back in ten minutes.
practice.why: have lunch is an action, so the Continuous is fine.
A state verb takes do/does in questions.

practice.q: He ___ that film — it's his favourite.
practice.why: love is a state verb.

practice.q: I ___ the sea from my window.
practice.why: see = perceive is a state.
need is a state verb.

title: at / on / in
summary: Which preposition goes with clock times, days and longer periods.

rules.name: at
rules.form: at + clock time or fixed expression
rules.when: A point on the clock, plus a small set of set phrases.

examples.en: at 7 o'clock, at half past six
examples.uk: о сьомій, о пів на сьому

examples.en: at night, at the weekend, at lunchtime

rules.name: on
rules.form: on + day or date
rules.when: A particular day or date.

examples.en: on Monday, on weekdays
on 14 May, on my birthday

rules.name: in
rules.form: in + longer period
rules.when: Parts of the day, months, seasons, years.

examples.en: in the morning, in July, in winter, in 2026

mistakes.note: in the morning / afternoon / evening, but at night
no preposition before every day, today, tomorrow, next week
days always take on

quiz.q: I get up ___ half past six.

practice.why: Clock times take at.
Months take in.
Days take on.
Parts of the day take in — except night.
at night is a fixed expression.
Years take in.
Dates take on.
British English uses at the weekend.
at lunchtime is a fixed expression.
every day takes no preposition.

title: Telling the time
summary: past and to, quarters and halves, and the trap for Ukrainian speakers.

rules.name: past and to
rules.form: minutes past the hour (1–30) · minutes to the next hour (31–59)
rules.when: Up to half past we count from the hour; after that we count to the next hour.

examples.en: 9:20 — twenty past nine
9:50 — ten to ten

rules.name: quarters and halves
rules.form: (a) quarter past · half past · (a) quarter to
rules.when: The usual British way of saying :15, :30 and :45.

examples.en: 7:30 — half past seven
8:45 — a quarter to nine

mistakes.note: in English half past seven = 7:30; half eight in speech means 8:30
o'clock is only used for a full hour

practice.why: Minutes 1–30 are counted past the hour.
After half past we count to the next hour.
half past + the hour that has passed.
20 minutes after six.
Five minutes before ten.
o'clock is used only for a full hour.
10 minutes after seven.
After 30 we count to the next hour.
15 minutes after twelve.
In English half past five = 5:30.

title: Present Continuous for plans
summary: Arrangements you have already agreed with someone use the Present Continuous.

rules.name: Arrangements
rules.form: am / is / are + -ing + future time expression
rules.when: The plan is already agreed and, in effect, in your diary.

examples.en: I'm meeting Marta at six tomorrow.
examples.uk: Я зустрічаюся з Мартою завтра о шостій.

examples.en: My cousin is coming to stay next week.
examples.uk: Наступного тижня приїжджає мій двоюрідний брат.

rules.name: Timetables stay Simple
rules.form: Present Simple
rules.when: Buses, trains, lessons and films run on a timetable, not on your agreement.

examples.en: The train leaves at 7:45.

mistakes.wrong: I meet Marta tomorrow at six.
mistakes.right: I'm meeting Marta tomorrow at six.
mistakes.note: an arrangement with another person takes the Continuous

mistakes.wrong: The train is leaving at 7:45 every day.
mistakes.note: a timetable takes the Present Simple

quiz.q: The film ___ at eight — it's on the website.
We ___ to the cinema on Friday after all.

practice.q: I ___ my cousin at the weekend — we agreed yesterday.
practice.why: An arrangement with someone takes the Continuous.

practice.q: The train ___ at 6:15 — it's on the timetable.
practice.why: Timetables take the Present Simple.
Asking about plans already made.

practice.q: We ___ to the seaside next week. The tickets are booked.
practice.why: A confirmed arrangement.

practice.q: The film ___ at nine, so let's meet at half past eight.
practice.why: A schedule takes the Simple.

practice.q: She ___ the dentist tomorrow at four.
practice.why: An appointment is an arrangement.

practice.q: They ___ tonight — they changed their minds.
practice.why: A cancelled arrangement takes the Continuous.
A timetable takes the Simple.
The Continuous question takes are.

practice.q: Which one is an arrangement, not a timetable?
options: I'm having lunch with Max at one.
practice.why: Lunch with a person is agreed, not scheduled by anyone else.

title: How long does it take?
summary: A fixed pattern for talking about how much time something needs.

rules.name: The pattern
rules.form: How long does it take (you) to + infinitive?  /  It takes (me) + time + to + infinitive.
rules.when: Asking and saying how much time an activity needs.

examples.en: How long does it take you to get ready?
examples.uk: Скільки часу тобі треба, щоб зібратися?

examples.en: It takes me twenty minutes to walk to school.
examples.uk: Мені треба двадцять хвилин, щоб дійти до школи.

rules.name: Negative and right now
rules.form: It doesn't take me long … / How long is it taking you?
rules.when: The same pattern in the negative, and in the Continuous for something happening now.

examples.en: It doesn't take me long to fall asleep.

mistakes.wrong: How long do you go to school?
mistakes.right: How long does it take you to get to school?
mistakes.note: the subject of the pattern is it, not you

mistakes.wrong: It takes me twenty minutes for walk.
mistakes.right: It takes me twenty minutes to walk.
mistakes.note: to + infinitive, not for

quiz.q: How long ___ it take you to get ready?
It ___ me an hour to do my homework.
It ___ take me long to fall asleep.

practice.q: How long ___ it take you to get to school?
practice.why: The subject is it → does.

practice.q: It ___ me an hour to do my homework.
practice.why: A regular fact takes the Simple.

practice.q: It ___ take me long to get ready.
practice.why: The Simple negative takes doesn't.

practice.q: It takes me twenty minutes ___ to school.
practice.why: to + infinitive.

options: How long do you go to school?
How long does it take you to get to school?
practice.why: The pattern needs it as the subject.

practice.q: How long ___ it take to cook rice?
practice.why: it → does.

practice.q: It ___ him two hours to finish the test.
practice.why: take → took in the past.

practice.q: ___ long does it take to get there by bus?
practice.why: How long asks about duration.

practice.q: It takes ___ ten minutes to warm up.
practice.why: The object pronoun goes straight after takes.

practice.q: How long is it ___ you to finish? You started an hour ago.
practice.why: The Continuous works for something still going on.

title: The three -ed sounds
summary: -ed is pronounced /t/, /d/ or /ɪd/ — and only the last one adds a syllable.

rules.name: /t/ after a voiceless sound
rules.form: walked · missed · stopped · watched · laughed
rules.when: After sounds like /k/, /s/, /p/, /tʃ/, /f/. No extra syllable.

examples.en: I walked home in the rain.

rules.name: /d/ after a voiced sound
rules.form: opened · called · arrived · realised · grabbed
rules.when: After vowels and voiced consonants. No extra syllable.

examples.en: She opened the door.

rules.name: /ɪd/ only after /t/ or /d/
rules.form: wanted · started · decided · needed · landed
rules.when: This is the only group that adds a whole syllable.

examples.en: We decided to walk instead.

mistakes.note: only /t/ and /d/ endings add a syllable
after t the ending is a full syllable

practice.why: After the voiceless /p/ the ending is /t/.
After /d/ the ending is a full syllable, /ɪd/.
After the voiced /l/ the ending is /d/.
After /f/ the ending is /t/.
After /t/ the ending adds a syllable.
After the voiced /z/ the ending is /d/.
After /s/ the ending is /t/.
After /d/ — a whole extra syllable.

practice.q: Which word has an extra syllable?
practice.why: Only /ɪd/ adds a syllable, and it follows t or d.
After the voiced /b/ the ending is /d/.

title: Strong adjectives
summary: freezing, starving, exhausted — words that already mean 'very'.

rules.name: They already contain 'very'
rules.form: cold → freezing · hungry → starving · tired → exhausted · angry → furious · wet → soaked · surprised → stunned
rules.when: Use them instead of very + ordinary adjective.

examples.en: I was absolutely freezing.
By lunchtime I was starving.
examples.uk: На обід я був страшенно голодний.

rules.name: Which intensifier
rules.form: very + ordinary · absolutely + strong
rules.when: very cold, but absolutely freezing.

examples.en: It was very cold. / It was absolutely freezing.
examples.uk: Було дуже холодно. / Було просто крижано.

mistakes.note: strong adjectives do not take very
ordinary adjectives do not take absolutely

practice.why: Strong adjectives take absolutely, not very.
cold is an ordinary adjective, so very.
starving already means very hungry.
soaked = wet right through.
furious already means very angry.
freezing already means very cold.

practice.q: He was ___ when he heard the news — he couldn't speak.
practice.why: stunned = too shocked to react.
A strong adjective never takes very.

practice.q: The exam is over — I feel ___.
practice.why: relieved = glad something bad has ended.

practice.q: There was an ___ silence after his question.
practice.why: awkward = uncomfortable and embarrassing.

title: Present Perfect: experiences
uk: Досвід у житті: have you ever…?
summary: Something has happened at some time in your life — when exactly doesn't matter.

rules.name: Form
rules.form:
have / has + past participle (V3)
I've seen · she's been · we haven't tried · Have you ever…?
rules.when: he / she / it → has; I / you / we / they → have. Regular verbs: V3 = -ed (visited). Irregular: learn the third form (been, seen, eaten).

examples.en: I've visited London twice.
She has never eaten sushi.

rules.name: ever and never
rules.form: Have you ever + V3 …? · I've never + V3 …
rules.when: ever = at any time in your life (questions). never = not at any time (it is already negative).

examples.en: Have you ever ridden a horse?
I've never been abroad.
examples.uk: Я ніколи не був за кордоном.

rules.name: Short answers
rules.form: Yes, I have. · No, I haven't. · Yes, she has. · No, she hasn't.
rules.when: Answer with have / has — never with the V3 and never 'Yes, I've.'

examples.en: Has your dad ever climbed a mountain? — Yes, he has.
examples.uk: Твій тато колись підіймався на гору? — Так.

rules.name: been or gone
rules.form: been to = went and came back · gone to = is there now
rules.when: For experiences we almost always use been.

examples.en: I've been to Kyiv three times.
examples.uk: Я тричі був у Києві (і повернувся).

examples.en: Max isn't here — he's gone to the shop.
examples.uk: Макса немає — він пішов у магазин (він ще там).

mistakes.wrong: Have you ever went to Italy?
mistakes.right: Have you ever been to Italy?
mistakes.note: after have / has comes the V3, not the Past Simple
V3 of eat is eaten
they → have
no short form at the end of a short answer
never is already negative

quiz.q: Has he ever won a prize? — Yes, he ___.

practice.why: Experience — you went and came back, so been.
After have you need the V3: ride – rode – ridden.
she → has.

practice.q: Has he ever won a prize? — Yes, he ___.
practice.why: Short answers use has / have, not the main verb.
She is at school now → gone.
never is already negative — no haven't.

practice.q: ___ your parents ever been to the sea in winter?
practice.why: parents = they → have.

practice.q: She has ___ three books this year.
practice.why: write – wrote – written.

practice.q: Which answer is correct? Have you ever broken a bone?
practice.why: No contraction at the end of a short answer.

practice.q: I've ___ Japanese food, but I didn't like it.
practice.why: Regular verb: the V3 is the same as the Past Simple — tried.

title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
uk: Коли досвід, а коли конкретний момент у минулому
summary: No time → Present Perfect. A finished time (yesterday, last summer, in 2020, when I was ten) → Past Simple.

rules.name: The one question to ask
rules.form: no time said → Present Perfect  ·  finished time → Past Simple
rules.when: If you can answer 'When?' with a finished time, it's the Past Simple.

examples.en: I've been to Lviv.
examples.uk: Я був у Львові (колись, неважливо коли).

examples.en: I went to Lviv last summer.
examples.uk: Я їздив до Львова минулого літа.

rules.name: The conversation pattern
rules.form: Have you ever…? → Yes, I have. → When / Where / Who / How did you…?
rules.when: Open with the Present Perfect, then switch to the Past Simple for the details.

examples.en: Have you ever broken a bone? — Yes, I have. I broke my arm when I was nine.
examples.uk: Ти колись ламав кістку? — Так. Я зламав руку, коли мені було дев'ять.

rules.name: Time words
rules.form:
PP: ever · never · before · so far · this year · twice
PS: yesterday · last week · in 2019 · ago · when I was…
rules.when: 'this year' / 'today' are not finished yet → Present Perfect. Questions with When? always take the Past Simple.

examples.en: She's won three medals so far.
examples.uk: Поки що вона виграла три медалі.

examples.en: When did you start skateboarding?
examples.uk: Коли ти почав кататися на скейті?

mistakes.wrong: I have seen that film last week.
mistakes.right: I saw that film last week.
mistakes.note: last week is finished time → Past Simple
When? asks about a moment → Past Simple
experience in your whole life → Present Perfect

quiz.q: ___ you ever been to a concert?

practice.why: last week — finished time → Past Simple.

practice.q: ___ you ever been to a concert?
practice.why: ever + experience → Present Perfect.
When? asks for a moment → Past Simple.
so far = up to now → Present Perfect.
in 2019 — finished time.

practice.q: Have you ever been to Lviv? — Yes, I ___ there last summer.
practice.why: The detail with a time → Past Simple.

practice.q: I ___ this book twice — it's my favourite.
practice.why: Experience, no time said → Present Perfect.

practice.q: We ___ to the sea two years ago.
practice.why: ago → Past Simple.
Question about a moment in the past → Past Simple.

practice.q: I ___ my phone three times this year!
practice.why: this year isn't finished → Present Perfect.

title: just · already · yet
summary: Three small words that go with the Present Perfect when something is connected to now.

rules.name: just
rules.form: have / has + just + V3
rules.when: A very short time ago.

examples.en: The bus has just left!

rules.name: already
rules.form: have / has + already + V3
rules.when: Sooner than expected, or 'no need — it's done'.

examples.en: I've already seen this film.

rules.name: yet
rules.form: …haven't + V3 … yet · Have you + V3 … yet?
rules.when: Only in negatives and questions, at the end of the sentence.

examples.en: I haven't finished my project yet.
Have you done your homework yet?

mistakes.note: yet only in negatives and questions, at the end
already goes between have and the V3

quiz.q: The bus has ___ left — you missed it by a second.

practice.q: The bus has ___ left — you missed it by a second.
practice.why: A second ago → just.
Negative sentence → yet at the end.
It's done, earlier than you think → already.
Question → yet at the end.

practice.q: Mum has ___ come in — her coat is still wet.
practice.why: A very short time ago → just.
already goes between have and the V3.

practice.q: We've ___ bought the tickets, so we don't need to queue.
practice.why: It's done → already.
Negative → yet.

practice.q: I've ___ woken up — give me five minutes.
practice.why: A moment ago → just.

practice.q: ___ you seen the new video yet?
practice.why: yet goes with the Present Perfect.
